question.text: A PM constructs an immunized portfolio. The most common ACTIVE element required even in 'passive' immunization is:

answer.text: Rebalancing duration whenever yields move significantly

explanation.text: The Logic: Although immunization is introduced as a passive bond-portfolio strategy, the workbook clarifies that it is not passive like buy-and-hold: when interest rates change, the portfolio requires active management and duration must be readjusted to match the remaining maturity of the liability. The Trap: Daily trading, credit-quality changes, or currency hedging are not what immunization requires; the active element is specifically rebalancing portfolio duration after meaningful yield moves. Note: Page 340 introduces immunization as passive bond-portfolio management; page 342 explains the active duration-readjustment requirement.
